title: Ninth Word Fourth Point Great Cycles Of Time Dawn And Noon

questions.question: What everyday object is used to help explain the different prayer times?
questions.answer: A clock with different hands is used as the example.

questions.question: How do the hands of that object relate to each other?
questions.answer: They match each other in pattern, reflect each other, and move in order.

questions.question: In the passage, what in the world is compared to the seconds on a clock?
questions.answer: The coming and going of day and night.

questions.question: What is compared to the minutes on that great world-clock?
questions.answer: The years.

questions.question: What is compared to the hours on that great world-clock?
questions.answer: The stages of a person’s life.

questions.question: What is compared to the days on that great world-clock?
questions.answer: The long periods in the life of the world.

questions.question: What part of the day is Fajr connected with in nature?
questions.answer: It is linked with early spring.

questions.question: What two beginnings in human life and creation does Fajr remind the reader of?
questions.answer: It points to a baby’s beginning in the womb and the first stage of creation.

questions.question: What does the time of Fajr help a person remember about Allah?
questions.answer: It helps a person remember Allah’s actions at those beginning stages.

questions.question: Which season is Zuhr compared to?
questions.answer: Midsummer.

questions.question: Which part of human life is Zuhr linked with?
questions.answer: The strongest time of youth.

questions.question: What does Zuhr call to mind besides summer and youth?
questions.answer: It reminds a person of a stage in human creation in the life of the world and of Allah’s mercy and many blessings.

questions.question: What big idea connects the examples of Fajr and Zuhr?
questions.answer: Prayer times remind people of other important times and help them think about Allah’s works, mercy, and blessings.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a clock before talking about prayer times?
questions.answer: To show that different time periods are connected and can point to one another.

questions.question: What are the four time-measures named on the clock?
questions.answer: Seconds, minutes, hours, and days.

questions.question: In the comparison, what takes the place of seconds?
questions.answer: Day and night changing one after another.

questions.question: In the comparison, what takes the place of minutes, hours, and days?
questions.answer: Years, the stages of a human life, and the long ages of the world.

questions.question: According to the passage, how are these time periods related?
questions.answer: They are alike in some ways, they remind people of each other, and they point to larger patterns.

questions.question: What time of day is Fajr in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the early morning before sunrise.

questions.question: Name one season and one human-life event that Fajr brings to mind.
questions.answer: It brings to mind spring and the beginning of life in the womb.

questions.question: What early event in the world’s creation is linked with Fajr?
questions.answer: The first stage of the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What does this suggest about Fajr as a prayer time?
questions.answer: It is a time that especially fits thoughts about beginnings and Allah’s creating power.

questions.question: What time of day is Zuhr in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the time just after midday.

questions.question: What season and what age of life are connected with Zuhr?
questions.answer: Midsummer and the best years of youth.

questions.question: What does Zuhr especially call to mind about Allah?
questions.answer: His mercy and the many gifts He gives.

questions.question: How are Fajr and Zuhr similar in the way they are explained?
questions.answer: Both are tied to other times in nature and human life, and both help people remember Allah’s actions and favors.

questions.question: What main lesson is taught by comparing prayer times to parts of a clock?
questions.answer: The lesson is that prayer times are part of a wise order in creation and connect with many other important times.

questions.question: What does the passage say day and night do in the world-clock image?
questions.answer: They act like the smallest repeating unit in that picture, like seconds.

questions.question: What do years show in that same image?
questions.answer: They are like the minutes.

questions.question: What shows the hours in that image?
questions.answer: The stages of a human lifetime.

questions.question: What shows the days in that image?
questions.answer: The long ages of the world.

questions.question: What three things does Fajr especially resemble?
questions.answer: Early spring, the start of life in the womb, and the first stage of creation.

questions.question: What does Fajr help a believer think about beyond the time of day itself?
questions.answer: It helps the believer think about Allah’s acts in bringing things into being.

questions.question: What three things does Zuhr especially resemble?
questions.answer: Midsummer, the peak of youth, and a major stage in human creation in the world’s lifetime.

questions.question: What blessings are especially remembered at Zuhr?
questions.answer: Allah’s mercy and the many good things He gives.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a clock and the world?
questions.answer: The world is pictured like a huge clock made and ruled by Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the parts of time in that world-clock?
questions.answer: Smaller and larger time periods match each other and remind people of one another.

questions.question: Which changing event in daily life stands for the smallest unit in this comparison?
questions.answer: The turning of day into night and night into day.

questions.question: Which longer unit stands for the next level after that?
questions.answer: The years.

questions.question: What human experience is used to represent a larger level of time?
questions.answer: The stages of a person’s life.

questions.question: What very large span of time is also included in the comparison?
questions.answer: The long eras of the world.

questions.question: How is Fajr described in relation to sunrise?
questions.answer: It is the early part of the day before the sun rises.

questions.question: What season does Fajr resemble, and what does that tell us?
questions.answer: It resembles spring, showing that it is linked with new beginnings.

questions.question: What beginning in a person’s life is connected to Fajr?
questions.answer: The first forming of life in the mother’s womb.

questions.question: What beginning in the history of creation is connected to Fajr?
questions.answer: The earliest stage of the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: How is Zuhr placed in the day?
questions.answer: It comes just after the middle of the day.

questions.question: What season and age does Zuhr match?
questions.answer: It matches summer and the prime years of youth.

questions.question: What does Zuhr remind a person to notice from Allah?
questions.answer: His mercy and His many blessings.

questions.question: What idea do the clock hands teach before the prayer times are explained?
questions.answer: They teach that different levels of time work together in an ordered way.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the different periods of time do for one another?
questions.answer: They reflect one another, resemble one another, and bring one another to mind.

questions.question: What are the four world-time examples listed from smaller to larger?
questions.answer: Day and night, years, the stages of human life, and the eras of the world.

questions.question: What prayer time is discussed first in the examples?
questions.answer: Fajr.

questions.question: What part of the natural year is linked to Fajr?
questions.answer: The start of spring.

questions.question: What part of human life before birth is linked to Fajr?
questions.answer: The beginning of a baby’s life in the womb.

questions.question: What early event in the universe is also linked to Fajr?
questions.answer: The beginning stage of creation.

questions.question: What prayer time is discussed second in the examples?
questions.answer: Zuhr.

questions.question: What season and age are linked to Zuhr?
questions.answer: Summer and youth at its strongest point.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found in the things Zuhr points to?
questions.answer: Mercy and many blessings.

questions.question: What is one reason the passage compares prayer times with other times in life and the world?
questions.answer: To show that prayer times fit into a larger pattern made by Allah.

questions.question: In the opening comparison, what do the hands of a clock do that time periods in the world also do?
questions.answer: They relate to one another and point to one another in an ordered way.

questions.question: What daily change is treated like the quickest repeating movement in the world-clock picture?
questions.answer: The alternation of day and night.

questions.question: What larger measures of time are named after that?
questions.answer: Years, human life stages, and world eras.

questions.question: What does this growing order from small to large help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see links between everyday time and much bigger events.

questions.question: Which prayer time is tied to beginnings, and what are two examples?
questions.answer: Fajr; two examples are spring and the beginning of life in the womb.

questions.question: What does the creation example connected to Fajr add to its meaning?
questions.answer: It shows that Fajr is not only about one morning but also about great beginnings in creation.

questions.question: What does Fajr invite a believer to remember about Allah?
questions.answer: His acts of bringing things into existence.

questions.question: Which prayer time is tied to fullness and growth, and what are two examples?
questions.answer: Zuhr; two examples are midsummer and the peak of youth.

questions.question: What stage in the world’s story is also connected with Zuhr?
questions.answer: A stage of human creation in the lifetime of the world.

questions.question: What two gifts from Allah are especially remembered at Zuhr?
questions.answer: His mercy and His abundant blessings.

questions.question: How are Fajr and Zuhr different in the ideas they emphasize?
questions.answer: Fajr emphasizes beginnings, while Zuhr emphasizes fullness and blessings.

questions.question: What is a good main idea for the whole passage?
questions.answer: The prayer times are wisely chosen moments that remind people of important patterns in creation, life, and Allah’s mercy.
